review_mode: independent read-only source and supplied compile-log review; no builds or proof edits
checks: Event ordinary pays exactly its announced Nat amount; store uses actual source-shaped storageCharge false with explicit warm/original/current/new values. Nonstatic scope is encoded in pay, not silently assumed for arbitrary calls.
run executes the event list from head to tail, binding each actual returned meter into the next payment; no reorder of refunds or debits.
pay_success uses the previously proved conservative SSTORE sentry/execution/state bounds or literal ordinary subtraction. Signed refunds and state credit/spill behavior remain inside storageCharge.
Aggregate payment theorem requires only initial sumExec/sumState budgets. It derives head payment gates and tail funding from returned lower bounds, with no per-step funding assumptions.
Future refunds are not spent in advance: each event reserves its conservative debit, and any actual credit can only help the lower-bound invariant.
Induction applies to any finite list without a fixed length cap; append theorem preserves exact sequencing and failure behavior.
scope_limits: Event list is an explicit source-meter transcript, not a proven extraction from actual reference execution. Root must construct events in order from the same actual trace including terminal operation.
No checked Python numeric upper bounds, trace-hook behavior, or executable reference refinement are proved.
State reservoir budget avoids needing execution spill for these sufficient conditions; this is conservative, not exact minimal resource usage.
Standalone pay_success has local budget premises, but the public aggregate payment producer derives those premises solely from initial totals.
